name: Digital Communication and Information Systems
description: Signal representation and LTI systems, Fourier transform and spectral properties, signal spaces, Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization, sampling theorem, quantization, Baseband modulation and pulse shaping, digital modulation schemes (M-ASK, M-PSK, M-FSK, M-QAM etc), pre-emphasis and de-emphasis filters, equalization and receiver design (matched filtering), probability and random variables, random processes, frequency domain representation of noise (power spectral density), noise performance analysis of digital modulation schemes, BER calculations. Introduction to source coding, Huffman coding, the asymptotic Equipartition property (AEP), Shannon’s theorem, channel capacity, bandwidth-S/N tradeoff.
